character.name: Fergus Oddfellow
character.description: A long-limbed figure who has clearly been assembled in a hurry under a hat that has seen service, holding a clipboard like a shield. Fergus is a Umbrella Lender and lends umbrellas against a deposit and has views on people who bring them back dry.

npc.narrative: You reach the cancello of The Polite Paddock, sotto a sky of stelle. Fergus Oddfellow stands behind a tavolo of umbrellas, smiling the way a man lifts a piano. A rubber stamp waits near his mano, unused and hopeful.
npc.native: Buonasera! Sono Fergus e presto ombrelli. Tutti chiedono che tempo fa, ma stasera ci sono le stelle. Come ti chiami?
npc.translation: Good evening! I am Fergus and I lend umbrellas. Everyone asks what the weather is like, but tonight there are stars. What is your name?

player: Buonasera Fergus, mi chiamo Sam. Ma che tempo fa domani? Io ho bisogno di un ombrello?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start, Sam! You introduced yourself, asked about the weather and even asked if you need an umbrella, all in clear Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: You asked Fergus about the weather correctly in Italian.

npc.narrative: Sotto le stelle, Fergus smiles with great effort and taps his timbro on the banco, not using it. Behind him the ombrelli wait, tutti dry and faintly offended.
npc.native: Piacere, Sam! Domani non lo so, ma un ombrello è sempre una buona idea. Ogni stagione ha la sua pioggia, e non so quale stagione è la peggiore. Che cosa fai tu quando piove?
npc.translation: Pleased to meet you, Sam! I do not know about tomorrow, but an umbrella is always a good idea. Every season has its own rain, and I do not know which season is the worst. What do you do when it rains?

player: Quando piove io resto a casa e guardo la TV. Ieri pioveva molto, tutto il giorno! Tu eri dove?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely work, Sam! You told Fergus what you do when it rains, said it rained yesterday, and even asked him a question back.

objectiveResults.feedback: This one wasn't asked yet: you need to ask Fergus which season he likes best. Fergus will give you another chance to ask it later.
Well done, "Ieri pioveva molto" tells Fergus clearly what the weather was like yesterday.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Fergus which season they like best, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Behind the banco, Fergus nods, timbro in mano, under a cielo full of stelle. The ombrelli in the rack stand perfectly asciutti, and he regards them with something close to sospetto.
npc.native: Resti a casa, che bella idea! Io ieri ero qui, con gli ombrelli e il mio timbro. Non so quale stagione è la migliore per un timbro, ma la primavera è molto bagnata. Che cosa fai tu quando c'è il sole?
npc.translation: You stay at home, what a nice idea! Yesterday I was here, with the umbrellas and my stamp. I don't know which season is the best for a stamp, but spring is very wet. What do you do when it is sunny?

player: Quando c'è il sole vado al parco. Ieri ha piovuto. Quale stagione ti piace di più?

verdict.overallFeedback: Bravo, Sam! You told Fergus what you do when it's sunny, said it rained yesterday, and asked about his favourite season, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked Fergus which season he likes best.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Quale stagione ti piace di più?

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you said it rained yesterday.

npc.narrative: Fergus lifts the timbro, studies you, and sets it down again, un po' sad. Above the banco the stelle are out, and not one of them is wet. On the ganci, a row of ombrelli waits for rain that has been postponed.
npc.native: Il parco, che bella idea! A me piace l'autunno, perché la gente riporta gli ombrelli bagnati. Un ombrello asciutto non è onesto. Che cosa fai tu al parco?
npc.translation: The park, what a lovely idea! I like autumn, because people bring the umbrellas back wet. A dry umbrella is not honest. What do you do at the park?

player: Al parco leggo un libro e mangio un gelato. Ma il mio ombrello è asciutto... sono onesto?

npc.narrative: Fergus lifts his timbro from the bancone, looks at it, and puts it down again with visible regret. Above the stalls le stelle are out, and one ombrello on its hook hangs very dry and rather guilty.
npc.native: Un libro e un gelato, che bel programma! Un ombrello asciutto non è onesto, ma tu sei una brava persona. Io sorrido, ma il timbro aspetta. Che libro leggi adesso?
npc.translation: A book and an ice cream, what a nice plan! A dry umbrella is not honest, but you are a good person. I smile, but the stamp waits. What book are you reading now?

player: Leggo un libro di Harry Potter, in italiano! È difficile. Perché il timbro aspetta?

npc.narrative: The notte is quiet. Fergus lifts the timbro from the banco, looks at it, and sets it down like a uomo refusing dessert. Above the tetto the stelle are out, and one ombrello in the angolo stays dry and under suspicion.
npc.native: Harry Potter in italiano, bravo! Il timbro aspetta perché cerco un buon motivo, e un ombrello asciutto è quasi un motivo. Ti piace la storia?
npc.translation: Harry Potter in Italian, well done! The stamp waits because I am looking for a good reason, and a dry umbrella is almost a reason. Do you like the story?

player: Sì, mi piace molto. Ok, è tardi. Buonanotte Fergus, a domani!

npc.narrative: Sopra the shop the stelle are out, and the lampada makes a small cerchio on the bancone. Fergus holds his timbro the way other uomini hold a cappello at a funerale. His sorriso arrives a moment after the rest of him, under protest.
npc.native: Ti piace molto, bene! Sì, è tardi, e le stelle sono belle. Domani il mio timbro aspetta ancora. Che cosa fai domani mattina?
npc.translation: You like it a lot, good! Yes, it is late, and the stars are beautiful. Tomorrow my stamp is still waiting. What are you doing tomorrow morning?
